narr: Heavy rain associated with weakening Hurricane Henri caused significant flash flooding in New Jersey on the morning of August 22. Most of the flood damage was confined to the central part of the state. Rainfall amounts were as high as 4.0 to 9.5 inches.
ev: The Musconetcong River overflowed its banks, flooding a section of NJ Route 173 in Greenwich Township.
US Route 46 was closed in Parsippany-Troy Hills due to flooding.
Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Helmetta. Many residents were evacuated from their homes by boat. Numerous roads in the town were inundated.
Numerous roads were closed and vehicles were stuck in the flood waters in South River.
Minor flooding occurred along Lawrence Brook on the border between New Brunswick and East Brunswick.
Widespread street flooding on Long Beach Island from Harvey Cedars to Surf City. Sections of Long Beach Boulevard were closed.
Two vehicles were trapped in flood waters near the intersection of Leeward Road and Breakers Drive in Stafford Township, requiring water rescues.
US Route 22 in North Plainfield was closed due to flooding.
US Route 202 in Raritan Township was under water.
South Middlebush Road was closed at Blackwells Mills Road in Franklin Township due to flooding.
Flooding resulted in road closures near the Millstone River in Rocky Hill and Montgomery Township.
Rock Brook overflowed its banks in Montgomery Township, resulting in the closure of Hollow Road to the north of Grandview Road.
Flooding occurred along the Neshanic River in Raritan Township.
A water rescue took place on Paxson Avenue in Hamilton Township.
Water rescues took place on South Broad Street and on Mercer Street in Trenton.
US Route 130 was closed at Church Street in Robbinsville Township due to flooding.
NJ Route 36 was closed in part of Middletown Township and Highlands due to flooding.
NJ Route 18 was closed at Cranbury Road in East Brunswick Township due to flooding.
US Route 1 in Edison Township was closed due to flooding.
Jersey Avenue in New Brunswick and North Brunswick Township was closed due to flooding.
Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Spotswood. Many roads were closed including Old Stage Road at Summerhill Road.
Flash flooding occurred on the Garden State Parkway southbound, north of Interchange 123 in Sayreville.
Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Milltown. Numerous roads were closed. Vehicles were submerged in the flood waters. A business and several houses were damaged.

A vehicle was trapped in flood waters on Woodland Drive in Plainsboro Township, requiring a water rescue. Another water rescue took place on Dey Road. Plainsboro Pond overflowed, closing Maple Avenue.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Manalapan Township and in Englishtown. Numerous roads in Manalapan Township were closed including Spotswood-Englishtown Road, Wilson Avenue, Sobechko Road, Union Hill Road and Conmack Lane. Main Street in Englishtown was closed due to flooding.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Cranbury Township. Numerous roadways were inundated and there were several water rescues. Brainerd Lake overflowed its banks, closing Main Street. A water rescue took place on Old Trenton Road.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in East Windsor Township and in Hightstown. Numerous roads were closed due to flooding. Water rescues took place along Hankins Road near Woodland Drive, and at the intersection of Mercer Street and Airport Road in East Windsor Township. US Route 130 was closed to the south of Princeton-Hightstown Road in East Windsor Township. Franklin Street was closed to the east of North Main Street in Hightstown.

The Millstone River overflowed its banks in West Windsor Township, inundating several roads. Grovers Mill Pond overflowed its banks in West Windsor Township, flooding several roads and damaging nearby buildings.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Jamesburg. Homes and businesses were severely damaged by the flood waters. Many roads were inundated and numerous water rescues took place. Some of the worst of the flooding occurred along Forsgate Drive in the area of Railroad Avenue. Homes near Manalapan Brook were evacuated.

Widespread flash flooding occurred in South Brunswick Township. US Route 130 was closed between Georges Road and Deans Rhode Hall Road. A water rescue took place on Ridge Road. US Route 1 was closed at Raymond Road. Herrod Boulevard was closed with vehicles stranded in the flood waters, requiring several water rescues.

Widespread and significant flash flooding occurred in Monroe Township. About 95 houses in the Rossmoor development were impacted by the flood waters, with many of the structures sustaining quite a bit of damage. Numerous roads in the township were closed and many vehicles were stranded in the flood waters. A section of NJ Route 33 to the east of Applegarth Road was closed.
